records.text: Owens said Charlie Kirk and Michael McCoy arrived in one Yukon Denali driven by a security person known only as Christopher.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Anyway, we still do not, however, have a positive ID on a rather crucial character, Christopher (security driver; surname unverified), the security member that was on Charlie (Charlie Kirk) and who drove him to the event at UVU with Mikey McCoy (Michael McCoy) and Nate Walker and Frank Turek in the backseat. Now, I want to show you guys some clearer images of Christopher (security driver; surname unverified) because I realized yesterday we only showed you one blurry one and I intended to show you.

Now, to the right of them, we have back-to-back Yukon Denalis. You, of course, know that one of the front is going to be the one that Charlie Kirk shows up in and that Charlie Kirk is going to depart in after he is hit with an explosive. ... And we know that he shows up with Mikey McCoy (Michael McCoy) in that vehicle. And we also know that the person driving it, we only have a first name for this guy. ... But his name is Christopher (security driver; surname unverified), okay? We're going to talk more about this Chris (Christopher; security driver; surname unverified) guy in a second.

records.text: Owens interpreted footage as showing Christopher, the security driver whose surname is unverified, and Nate Walker upstairs near the Sorensen building minutes before Kirk was struck, away from Kirk’s vehicle.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: and then makes a decision to go upstairs with Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s assistant, Nate Walker, heading toward the Sorensen Center. ... Just before the bang, I mean, minutes before the bang.

Yet Christopher (security driver; surname unverified), for some odd reason, Minutes before Charlie (Charlie Kirk) gets hit, he decides to go upstairs with Nate Walker, and he is upstairs when the shot goes off. So Chris (Christopher; security driver; surname unverified), the security person who has the keys, who locks the car, is upstairs when the explosive goes off. ... We're now we're putting a little white thing on that. That's Chris (Christopher; security driver; surname unverified) in the front. And you're going to see behind him, that's Nate. ... So he's upstairs and Nate is upstairs when the explosive goes off. Again, this is minutes before the explosive goes off. What were they doing? Where were they? ... Why were they headed toward the Sorensen building? At this moment, nobody knows, okay? But it's relevant. What could there be to do toward the Sorensen building on a campus that you've never been to when Charlie (Charlie Kirk) specifically expressed?

records.text: Owens speculated that the keys were apparently waiting in Kirk’s vehicle or somehow given to Justin Davis beforehand, while saying she did not know.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Someone just turned on the car. Now, in order for them to drive that vehicle off, of course, the keys were either already in the car or it was in one of their pockets as well. It could have been in Justin Davis's ... Pocket. It could have been in Blake (security team member; surname unverified)'s pocket. Blake (security team member; surname unverified) could have put it in the car. And I will say from a purely speculative standpoint that it is at least plausible that in the immediate aftermath of the explosion, one of them either already had the keys on them or perhaps were handed the keys. Because if you watch the footage from Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s front, after the explosive goes off, both Justin (Justin Davis) and Blake (security team member; surname unverified), ... um, at first sort of slide and dive toward Charlie (Charlie Kirk) before then instantly pivoting and sprinting to the car. And we're going to isolate those actions and show you that one by one. First up, we're going to look at Blake (security team member; surname unverified). Okay, so he is going to dive across the table. That's our table diver. You can watch him actually from two angles. We have the angle behind Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s head, which Terryl (Terryl Farnsworth) shared with me, and the angle from the crowd. Take a look at this. There ... Who knows how those keys got there or whether or not the keys were given or when exactly the keys were given rather to Justin (Justin Davis) or Blake (security team member; surname unverified). ... Unless one or both of them wants to come forward and share their stories or fill in some of these holes, we can't know for certain.

All the more reason to lock it, right? Well, I'm now going to show you some more never-before-seen footage from that day so you can remark, as I have, how smooth and convenient it all is that keys were apparently either waiting in the car or somehow given to Justin Davis before this. ... I don't know, but I'm going to show you this footage multiple times, and I'm going to highlight different portions.

records.text: Owens said footage showed Justin Davis sprinting to the vehicle and opening the passenger door beside a security participant named Blake whose surname is unverified; neither had arrived in that vehicle.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And of course is the video that we showed you yesterday. And we are again going to isolate Justin Davis so that you can see that he is the first to arrive with Blake (security team member; surname unverified) in tow to the open passenger door of the Denali.

Again, this is not Justin Davis' car, but he immediately sprints ahead to the vehicle and opens the passenger side door alongside Blake (security team member; surname unverified), who is also not in this vehicle.

records.text: Owens interpreted footage as showing Danny Philip and Michael McCoy converging and ducking in front of Kirk’s vehicle with Justin Davis after the shooting.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Just before the bang, I mean, minutes before the bang. And like I said, some people thought that maybe it's Mikey (Michael McCoy) who handed those keys to Justin Davis because Mikey (Michael McCoy) was, in fact, in the car. Maybe he had a spare set during that little front-of-car powwow. Maybe. I do think it's odd that both Danny (Danny Philip) and Mikey (Michael McCoy) instantly went to that exact spot, separately but instantly, especially Danny (Danny Philip), because Danny (Danny Philip) didn't arrive in that car. ... Danny (Danny Philip)'s passing his car and then goes right in the front and does that little dip and then goes off with Mikey (Michael McCoy) to the left.

show you this little company powwow if you want to call it that a little little company meeting that takes place for a couple of seconds I'm going to draw your attention to the amazing Mikey McCoy (Michael McCoy) who we are told repeatedly was definitely not on his phone and was just covering his ear for noise well he's going to keep on covering his ear for noise but remarkably if you look at him and Danny Philip Despite not being with each other, they were on opposite sides of Charlie (Charlie Kirk), ... both of them are going to kind of run and then meet each other in front of Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s vehicle and duck down for a little meet and greet with Justin Davis, like a perfect little dip and meet as if they all knew to go there.

records.text: Owens said she thought the bag left behind belonged to Christopher, explicitly stating she was not 100 percent certain and was reasoning by elimination.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: expressed yesterday that I believe the backpack belongs to Chris (Christopher, security driver; surname unverified), the anonymous Chris (Christopher, security driver; surname unverified), and ... I am inferring upon some other evidence that I have been withholding that I'm going to share with you all today.

I think that that's Chris (Christopher; security driver; surname unverified)'s bag. ... I think, again, I will say not 100% certain that it's his bag, but given the fact that Mikey McCoy (Michael McCoy) showed up with a bag and has it on his back and just process of elimination here, I think that's going to be the security person's bag.

records.text: Owens said Brian Harpole told Shawn Ryan there had been no threats the night before Kirk’s death, and said this conflicted with associates now acknowledging Kirk feared he would die.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Also, it's interesting that Brian Harpole's claim, as he told Shawn Ryan, [unclear aside about pulling it from the episode], was that Charlie (Charlie Kirk) had no fears night before. But now Turning Point USA is disputing that. ... They're now saying that he did have fears and communicated them to his security team. That registers to me as incompetence. You're suing me for saying the security team is incompetent. Well, why wasn't that expressed to everybody on the team?

suddenly because they're just getting antsy and they're like oh Charlie (Charlie Kirk) did think he was going to die and it's like well Brian Harpole said there were no threats the night before he was sitting down with Shawn Ryan he was like no nothing so there just seems to be this constant conflict between what various people on the security team and at Turning Point USA recall anyway we will leave it at that we will see you guys tomorrow

records.text: Owens identified a man in a security photograph as Todd Espy; the episode does not independently authenticate that identification.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: We now know that that is Todd Espy, like I said, bright blue shirt, far right, just in front of Alex Faria and Brian Harpole.

records.text: Owens said she was fairly certain a security participant called Chester went by Claude Barnes and was affiliated with Integrity Security Solutions.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And then we had remaining the person Chester (host tentatively identifies this person as Claude Barnes), I think he goes by Claude Barnes. Now, we're fairly certain we've done our bit of research here that that is Claude Barnes. He is at least with Integrity or was with Integrity Solutions.

records.text: Owens said unnamed people connected with Turning Point USA told her Christopher was hired in late 2024 and allegedly attended the Hamptons event where Netanyahu called in; she did not establish his surname.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Now, I can tell you that I did, of course, reach out to my sources at Turning Point USA to learn more about him. ... When was he hired? Who is he? I don't recognize him. And I was told that he was hired late 2024. ... and that he was not particularly friendly. He didn't speak to anyone at Turning Point USA's facilities. He was on Charlie (Charlie Kirk), and so that's why nobody seems to know his last name. ... And I was also told that he was allegedly in attendance during that fateful Hamptons summit where Bibi Netanyahu (Benjamin Netanyahu) called Charlie Kirk something, a story that we broke and which, I mean, Erika (Erika Kirk) confirmed the reasons for that phone.

records.text: Owens inferred that the SUV was already unlocked because Justin Davis ran directly to its door and opened it without visible flashing lights; she did not establish where its keys were.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They go directly to the passenger side door and it does not appear that it is locked, okay? ... How do we know? Because if they had unlocked the door on their way while they were running, we would see that in the footage. ... The backlights would flash as backlights do when you hit the car keys open on any modern car. ... And this is a 2025 Denali. So we know that it would just, you know, look red, and we'd go,

records.text: Owens interpreted footage as showing a security participant named Blake reaching toward his pocket with a small object, while saying she could not tell whether it was a key.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: he is. There's Blake (security team member; surname unverified). You're going to see him kind of jump across the table there, and many people looked at that and thought it was possible that there was a handoff of some description. But actually, if you examine some side footage, which I'm about to show you, it looks more like he reaches into his pocket for something, something that we can deduce has to be small because he uses just two fingers. ... We have no idea if it's a car key. It could also be something else entirely, but we're just showing you all of this because, you know, all of these little pieces make up a puzzle. ... Maybe keys, maybe not, maybe something totally different. Can't be certain, worth noting. Next up, we have Justin Davis.

records.text: Owens said the movements around Kirk’s vehicle looked strangely choreographed to her; this was her interpretation of the footage.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It's obviously chaotic, but it's also strangely choreographed, in my view, right? ... It's strange to me that there doesn't seem to be any misdirection or any fumbling or any confusion. ... They all knew to go to that car specifically. They knew it was available. They knew it was open. ... Again, this is all happening within 45 seconds. This is happening within 30 seconds when you see Justin (Justin Davis) and them get there.

records.text: Owens identified the person who fell from the rear of Kirk’s SUV while a backpack fell out as Alex Faria, whose identity remains unverified.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That is Alex Faria. OK, Alex Faria, it looks as though he attempts to get into the trunk where Frank Turek is, but then he falls out and we can show you that. ... that with Alex Faria isolated. And yes, in addition to that, you will see in this clip a backpack falls out of the car. Take a look here. There ... is Alex (Alex Faria). He gets in, and ... then the backpack falls out at the end there.

records.text: Owens said she did not believe the account that Frank Turek performed CPR in the SUV and thought Brian Harpole was telling the truth when he said he had not performed CPR.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Now, I do want to say regarding Alex Faria falling out of that car, it's a bit of a wonder that a pastor would think it's wise for him to be in the car above security on the way to the hospital. You would think that he would yield to security and say, OK, I'll find my own way. ... I think that feels mildly inappropriate, given the circumstances. And speaking of Frank Turek, there are a lot of things that he has said about that day that are questionable. I mean, definitely the CPR, the CPR story to me is the most senseless. ... His excuse that Brian Harpole was distracted and forgot that he conducted CPR on a dying person in the veh— ... In the very small vehicle, I don't think Harpole (Brian Harpole) just forgot that. I actually think Harpole (Brian Harpole) told the truth between the two of them, if I'm being honest, when he said that no CPR was conducted in the car. I don't think he was distracted.

records.text: Owens identified the woman who retrieved the backpack after the shooting as Chrissy Pacheco, a Turning Point USA logistics employee.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It is, again, more remarkable luck. It looks like choreography almost. They're so lucky that it happened to be a longtime Turning Point USA employee, Chrissy Pacheco, who picks up that backpack. ... It's not a random student or a passerby or police officer, but a person that was in charge of logistics on that day, a member of the logistics team for Turning Point USA that helped to set up everything. ... That is the truth of the answer. She's there in time just to pick up the backpack as it falls out, and I can show, we can show that again if we want to just show that clip of the backpack falling out and then it's sort of getting scooped by Chrissy (Chrissy Pacheco). Here we go. Here comes the backpack. We've highlighted Chrissy (Chrissy Pacheco) there, so you can see first ... thing she does is she picks up that backpack. End of story. Just in case you guys thought it was a rando, it's not a rando, someone on the Turning Point USA team.

records.text: Owens said newly presented footage around 12:11 p.m. on September 10 showed Christopher accessing the SUV’s trunk, about twelve minutes before Kirk was shot; she could not determine exactly what he handled.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Something interesting that happened could be interesting. I think it's interesting. You see, around 12:11 p.m., so like approximately 12 minutes before Charlie (Charlie Kirk) gets hit. ... Chris (Christopher, security driver; surname unverified), a person that's supposed to be on Charlie (Charlie Kirk) with keys in hand, heads to that Denali and he unlocks the trunk and he either puts something into the trunk or takes something out of whatever is in the trunk. ... That part is obvious. There's something in the trunk that he is going, as you will see, to, I guess you could say, fumble around with. ... No one's around. And he goes right where the backpack maybe is. Looks like he almost put something in his pocket. ... Looks to the left a little suspiciously. ... Let's play it again for people back at home. ... Here he is. ... There he goes. ... Something on that left side. ... Again, this is approximately 12:11. Put something in his pocket. Looks back to make sure no one is looking at him.

records.text: Owens said Andrew Kolvet authorized Andrew Wilson to read an alleged Telegram exchange involving Kirk in a debate opening without displaying it, and said Turning Point USA had not authenticated it.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Anyway, so while I was in Iceland, Turning Point USA, namely Andrew Kolvet, greenlit Andrew Wilson coming out with an alleged Telegram message from Charlie Kirk the night before he was killed. ... Now, this is the same message that Andrew Wilson bizarrely read as his opening statement in our debate. ... Our debate was not about Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s messages the night before. Very strange that he would read that and then didn't want to show it during our debate. ... And then he released the alleged message on his show. Now, what's very strange about this, immediately strange, and should strike you as... ... very intentional is that Turning Point will not acknowledge its authenticity and that Turning Point did not choose to instead, since their whole narrative that they have been trying to push is that a leftist did this, why didn't they release this immediately? Why didn't Turning Point USA give this to New York Post, give this to the Daily Mail, say, aha, here it is, evidence that he was terrified of the left? No. To the contrary, they did the exact opposite.

records.text: Owens said a trusted unnamed source described Kirk’s message to Dan Flood as an iMessage saying they were going to kill him, rather than a Telegram message specifying the left.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I was the one who revealed, and I did not say the left because I was told it did not say the left. ... I was told that he said they are going to kill me to Dan Flood. And I have it on good authority also that the message went out to Dan Flood via iMessage, not Telegram, to strike you again as remarkably. ... What I didn't reveal to Erika (Erika Kirk) is that a source that I trust deeply, much more than I trust Erika (Erika Kirk), and who has been more consistent on telling the truth about what happened on that day, said the text messages were received on iMessage. ... So I am not inclined to believe that these messages are on Telegram.

records.text: Owens said she believed the exchange read by Wilson was a recreation in which the words the left had been added; she did not present authenticated message records establishing that allegation.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But you know what? Rather than me assert that I believe that the message is a recreation of a message that was sent on iMessage, not Telegram. ... sent to Dan Flood and with the words the left added, let's for a moment do what the defense does during a probative hearing. ... Let me actually engage in their arguments. Let's pretend for a moment the message is real because they made a very, very big mistake.

records.text: In the disputed exchange Owens read, a sender she tentatively identified as Dan Flood said the security plan included his team, campus police and backup patrol officers, with eleven people on site.
records.speaker: Dan Flood

appearances.snippet: And Charlie (Charlie Kirk) wants to know what's the lay of the land. Dan Flood comes back and says, yes, law enforcement has been fully supportive and has agreed to the security plan and posture. ... Tomorrow's event will be covered by both my team and campus PD. If additional support is required, patrol units will be available. ... And Charlie (Charlie Kirk) says, thank you. Threats are higher than ever. And then that gets cut off. And Dan (Dan Flood) says, I have 11 on site. ... Dan (Dan Flood) then comes back and says, just so you are aware, I will be, and I'm going to say Dan (Dan Flood) because that's what I was told. Remember, I'm the one who told you about these messages.

records.text: Owens said Erika Kirk acknowledged the fear messages were real during their private meeting and described connecting Charlie’s phone to the internet and its auto-delete settings; this is Owens’s account of that meeting.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Months later, we're supposed to believe that Erika (Erika Kirk) was completely ignorant on these messages until I clocked her. ... That was the original TPUSA sin, so to speak, that I said, that's really weird. And the next day I went on my show and I said, she's lying. ... Erika (Erika Kirk) was lying there. That's very strange. These messages absolutely were real. They were received by Dan Flood and Andrew Kolvet. ... And then I met up with Erika (Erika Kirk). They very quickly then reached out and she was like, oh yeah, no, the messages are real. ... Once you said that, then I went in and I saw that Charlie (Charlie Kirk), she said something about connecting it to the phone, to the internet. ... And she then confirmed with the team. And Charlie (Charlie Kirk) had the phone set to auto-delete on his Signal and his Telegram.

records.text: Owens said the fear messages were sent while Kirk was on a Zoom call about Israel, and cited a September 9 sequence involving Will Cain, Mark Halperin and a 3:54 p.m. message about leaving the pro-Israel cause.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But actually, there's something bigger, boys and girls, the trap that they walked right into. More interesting than this, whether or not the message is edited or not, is that Andrew Wilson provided timestamps. The internet literally did not clock this. ... Now, Andrew (Andrew Wilson), Andrew Wilson, if you had listened to me and how much I love a timeline, my official timeline, you would have recalled that I had been meticulous about Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s schedule on September 9th, every hour of what he was doing, but I could populate onto my official timeline, confirming his whereabouts, what he was doing. ... And what is interesting about when Charlie (Charlie Kirk) sent these alleged panicked messages to his security, Dan Flood, and to Andrew Kolvet, which he has not yet addressed, is that he sent them when he was on the now notorious Zoom call with leaders in Israel. ... Erika (Erika Kirk), remember, he comes back from Korea, so he's jet-lagged. Erika (Erika Kirk) said that she woke Charlie (Charlie Kirk) up for his Fox News hit. ... That's per Andrew Kolvet. At 1 o'clock p.m., Charlie (Charlie Kirk) appears in the Will Cain show from his Turning Point USA office studio. ... He then jumps right on to a 40-minute interview on Mark Halperin's show. At 3 o'clock p.m., Erika (Erika Kirk) told me that she was getting her nails done and that in this hour is when Charlie (Charlie Kirk) had that back and forth and fight on the phone and said that he was leaving the pro-Israel cause. ... And no, he was not saying it tongue in cheek. That's at 3:54 p.m. That message was sent.

records.text: Owens suggested the Zoom call might have been an emergency intervention over Kirk’s position on Israel and speculated that they in his alleged fear messages might refer to people on that call; the episode supplies no independent proof of that interpretation.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Suddenly, there's a Zoom call. An emergency Zoom call. It seems to be this was an emergency Zoom call because we have Charlie (Charlie Kirk), we have Josh Hammer, we have Frank Turek, we have Rabbi Wolicki (Pesach Wolicki). ... We have two Israeli officials that are on the Zoom call, as well as Blake Neff and Andrew Kolvet. If Rabbi Wolicki (Pesach Wolicki) is to be believed, he says that actually, we'll show you that in a second, that his producers were on the phone call. ... So I want you to picture that, okay, that during the time that he is on this phone, that he is on this Zoom call and Andrew Kolvet is on the Zoom call, Charlie (Charlie Kirk) texts him, texts Andrew (Andrew Kolvet), allegedly, as Andrew (Andrew Kolvet) told me, he told me this explicitly, he receives a text and says, they're going to kill me. ... And he says he doesn't know who he was referring to. But if you were on a Zoom call with Israeli officials after you said that you were leaving the pro-Israel cause, and Rabbi Wolicki (Pesach Wolicki) confirmed, by the way, he was the only one who told the truth. Everyone was like, this call was just daisies and it was about prepping. Rabbi Wolicki (Pesach Wolicki) actually said, yeah, it got a little contentious. Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was playing devil's advocate. Uh, you know, Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was pushing back, asking us about Gaza. ... If all of that is to be believed, because I said, why would Charlie (Charlie Kirk) just send you, they are going to kill me. ... No context. Well, the context might have been, Andrew (Andrew Kolvet), in reference to the Zoom call that you were on when this message was sent. ... You're on the phone. You say you text to someone. It's not going well. They're going to kill me. ... That might have been the they. If I was using my context clues, if I was in an English class and they said, who is the they that he is referencing in this moment, it would be who he was currently on the Zoom call with.

records.text: Frank Turek said he and Kirk participated in a Zoom meeting the day before Kirk’s death discussing how to answer arguments against Israel on campus, and said he was confident Kirk was not about to give up supporting Israel.
records.speaker: Frank Turek

appearances.snippet: So, the next day we had a meeting. ... a Zoom meeting with a couple of people in Israel and a couple of people in the room. ... and another person, an expert on Israel in the United States, and we were asking them, and Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was asking them, tell me your perspective on what's going on with Hamas now and the Israeli situation. ... Tell me, I want to be better able to answer questions when I get questions on this. So contrary to popular opinion, some popular opinion that Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was giving up on Israel, that's not true. ... He was trying to prepare himself to know the facts and be better able to answer those questions. ... This is the day before he was murdered. ... We're in this meeting. I'm in the meeting with him.

appearances.snippet: So the next day we get up, we fly up to Utah and he actually, we had to stop to do a. ... He was going to do a presentation to a group of restaurateurs because his cousin was a restaurateur and said, ... come speak to my group of restaurant owners? We stop at this.

records.text: Owens said Andrew Kolvet forwarded Kirk’s message about leaving the pro-Israel cause to Joe Kent and Tulsi Gabbard’s office.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: So there's what we have. Frank (Frank Turek) telling us a story that Charlie (Charlie Kirk) had written this text message, said that he was abandoning the pro-Israel cause, that he wanted to bring Candace (Candace Owens) back. ... They tried to turn this into some tongue-in-cheek text message. It wasn't that. Andrew (Andrew Kolvet) did not tell me it was that. ... Andrew (Andrew Kolvet) clearly was concerned enough about being on this text thread that he sent it to Joe Kent. ... When asked about threats and things, and he thought that this message was relevant enough to send. To Tulsi Gabbard's office to investigate further. ... It was not tongue-in-cheek because when I asked Erika (Erika Kirk) about this message, she didn't say it was tongue-in-cheek. ... Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was angry.

records.text: In the New York Post account read by Owens, Rabbi Pesach Wolicki described Kirk as combative and argumentative during the Zoom call, saying Kirk was playing devil’s advocate to prepare for debates.
records.speaker: Pesach Wolicki

appearances.snippet: Then we have from Rabbi Wolicki (Pesach Wolicki) that he kept up that energy. He said in various interviews, you can go back, we have shown it, that he he was the only one that told the truth that this call was not some peachy, oh, we just want some debating talking points, even when he spoke to the New York Post. ... He said, quote, he was working out talking points, playing the role of devil's advocates, devil's advocate, pushing up on these issues, trying to sharpen the iron. ... He was in a combative mood, he recalled, but that was good. Because he was preparing for debates and he was preparing for attacks.

conveyance.original_source: New York Post interview with Pesach Wolicki, quoted by Owens

records.text: Owens said Erika Kirk did not deny during their four-hour meeting that Charlie Kirk had been angry with his pastors and was done with the pro-Israel cause.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He was done with the pro-Israel cause.
